<!--
  Curated release highlights for the NEXT release. Maintainer-edited.
  `scripts/build-release-notes.mjs` prepends this verbatim as the "## Highlights"
  section of both the GitHub Release notes and the Version Packages PR body.
  Keep it SHORT: the few most important user-facing changes, ONE concise line
  each. The per-package sections below already carry the full detail — do NOT
  duplicate it here. Update (or clear) this file when cutting a new release.
-->
- **Project scaffolding** — the new `connectum init` scaffolds a production-ready project, interactively or fully from flags, composing only the modules you pick (OpenTelemetry, EventBus with an adapter, auth, service catalog, resilience), and `connectum generate service` adds a service with a starter proto and a `defineService` skeleton ([#229](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/229)).
- **Proto enums in scaffolded projects** — `connectum init` generates Protobuf enums as `as const` objects (`erasable_syntax=true`, protobuf-es `^2.16.0`), so a project whose protos declare enums type-checks and runs under Node's native type stripping ([#280](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/280)).
- **Option descriptors from the packages** — `@connectum/auth` and `@connectum/events` export their generated option descriptors (`./gen/connectum/{auth,events}/v1/options_pb.js`, the same module the package uses), and `connectum init --auth` / `--events` imports them via `map_imports` instead of generating local copies, flooring the whole `@connectum/*` set at `^1.3.0` ([#284](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/284)).
- **Shutdown that always finishes** — with the default `forceCloseOnTimeout`, `server.stop()` now closes every connection still open at the shutdown timeout on every transport (HTTP/1.1, h2c, TLS), so a stuck or GOAWAY-ignoring client can no longer keep the process alive; idle HTTP/2 clients are sent GOAWAY at the start of shutdown on every Node line.
- **Health stays SERVING across in-process calls** — the first `ctx.call` or `server.localClient()` no longer drops overall health to `NOT_SERVING`, reflection lists the same services in-process as over HTTP, and `defineLazyService` builds one instance per server; custom protocols move one-time work into the new `setup(context)` (**BREAKING** for custom `ProtocolRegistration` implementations only) ([#265](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/265)).
- **Reliable AMQP publishing** — opt-in `publishRetry` on `@connectum/events-amqp` auto-retries connection-class publish failures (never nacks/timeouts) with bounded backoff and honest at-least-once semantics ([#222](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/222)), and the new `drainPublishTimeout` on `@connectum/events` gives in-flight publishes a bounded drain window during `stop()` ([#220](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/220)).
- **amqplib 2.2.0 baseline** — `@connectum/events-amqp` now requires amqplib `^2.2.0`: reconnect delays of the built-in backoff never exceed `maxDelay` (amqplib's own reconnect loop, including the bounded initial connect, and the adapter's own `publishRetry` and consumer-restore delays), and once recovery gives up after its retry budget the adapter forgets the dead connection — `subscribe()`/`publish()` reject with a typed `AmqpConnectionError` instead of hanging or leaking a raw error, `publishRetry` stops at once, and `connect()` starts clean.
- **Custom AMQP reconnect backoff** — `recovery.backoff` on `@connectum/events-amqp` sets your own delay for every reconnect attempt, initial connect included, and a failing hook ends recovery with a typed `AmqpConnectionError` (no fallback to the built-in schedule); `initialConnectMaxRetries` is now served by amqplib's own initial budget on the connection the adapter keeps ([#301](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/301)).
- **Deterministic AMQP failure policy** — `initialConnectMaxRetries` bounds the first connect ([#219](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/219)), and `treatTopologyErrorAsFatal` stops infinite recovery on deterministic topology drift at runtime — only a `404`/`406` whose broker message names a missing or incompatible queue or exchange; self-healing and unrecognised replies stay in recovery ([#218](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/218)).
- **Observable AMQP lifecycle** — the new discriminated `onLifecycle` callback delivers the full connection-lifecycle event union in guaranteed order ([#216](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/216)), and `AmqpTopologyError` now carries a machine-readable `.object` identifying the failing exchange/queue/binding ([#217](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/217)).
- **AMQP faults you can see** — `@connectum/events-amqp` reports a delivery it could not settle on a closed channel (`settlement-skipped`) and a throwing or rejecting lifecycle callback (`lifecycle-error`) as lifecycle events instead of crashing on an unhandled rejection or swallowing them; `treatTopologyErrorAsFatal` now stops only on deterministic drift, `publishRetry` stops at once on a channel the broker closed, and `disconnected` carries the broker's close code with `recovery: false` ([#298](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/298)).
- **Broker-free AMQP testing** — the new `@connectum/events-amqp/testing` subpath ships a programmable `FakeAmqpAdapter`: FIFO publish outcomes with the real typed errors, a deterministic recovery control surface, and delivery with settlement counts ([#224](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/224)).
- **Typed adapter DI** — `@connectum/events` exports the `EventAdapterFactory` type for per-consumer adapter wiring and test seams ([#223](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/223)).
- **Reject before the body is read** — opt-in `requestGate` and `readMaxBytes` on `createServer()` set Connect's request gate and per-message read limit as server-wide defaults, applied identically over HTTP and in-process (no transport exemption) and overridable per service; HTTP requests can no longer show a gate a forged in-process marker; `server.stop()` now aborts in-flight in-process calls (`localClient`, `ctx.call`) exactly like HTTP ones (**BREAKING** behaviour for code that relied on local calls finishing undisturbed during shutdown) ([#281](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/281)).
- **`break` ends a streaming call** — leaving a `for await` loop over a streaming response now cancels the call (`@connectrpc/connect` 2.3.0): the handler's `signal` aborts and its `finally` runs, over HTTP and in-process alike.
- **Transport-tagged request logs** — opt-in `includeTransport` on `createLoggerInterceptor` tags every log line `[in-process]` or `[http]`, so `server.localClient()` calls are told apart from network calls at a glance; off by default, telemetry only ([#272](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/272)).
- **protobuf-es 2.16 and Connect 2.3 as peer dependencies** — the runtime `@connectum/*` packages declare `@bufbuild/protobuf` `^2.16.0` and `@connectrpc/connect` / `@connectrpc/connect-node` `^2.3.0` as peers (`@connectum/core` and `@connectum/testing`; the other packages accept `^2.2.0`, but every server runs `@connectum/core`), so your application and Connectum share one copy of each; generate code with `protoc-gen-es` 2.16. An out-of-range pin now fails the install on npm (`ERESOLVE`), and on every package manager `createServer()` refuses to start with a `PeerDependencyVersionError` naming the library and the fix (unless `@connectum/core` is bundled into your application, where the startup check is skipped), instead of running on a second or too-old copy (**BREAKING** for out-of-range pins — see the migration guide) ([#277](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/277), [#282](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/282)).
- **`connectum init` with pnpm + OpenTelemetry installs cleanly** — the generated `pnpm-workspace.yaml` now lists every dependency build script the modules bring in, so `--package-manager pnpm --otel` no longer fails its first install with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` on pnpm 11+ ([#279](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/279)).
- **Nameable OpenTelemetry provider** — `@connectum/otel` now exports the `OtelProvider` type that `getProvider()` returns, so you can store and pass the provider without `ReturnType<...>` ([#278](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/278)).
- **One OpenTelemetry provider, whichever subpath you import** — `@connectum/otel` subpaths (`/provider`, `/tracer`, `/meter`, ...) no longer carry private copies of the provider singleton, so mixing them with the root import no longer creates a second provider that fights the first over OpenTelemetry's global registration; `@connectum/core`, `@connectum/interceptors` and `@connectum/testing` share their modules across subpaths the same way.
- **OTLP/HTTP exporters work out of the box** — `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp/http` (and the metrics/logs equivalents) no longer throws `Could not parse user-provided export URL: 'undefined/v1/traces'` when no endpoint is set: the exporter falls back to `http://localhost:4318/v1/<signal>`. The standard value `otlp` is now accepted and follows `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` (`grpc`, `http/protobuf` — real protobuf on the wire, the specification default — or `http/json`), and for OTLP/HTTP a per-signal `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_<SIGNAL>_ENDPOINT` takes precedence over the base endpoint, as the OpenTelemetry environment contract says ([#310](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/310)).
- **Native gRPC Server Reflection** — `@connectum/reflection` and `connectum proto sync` no longer depend on `@lambdalisue/connectrpc-grpcreflect` (no stray second protobuf copy), and answers now follow the protocol: `grpcurl describe` of a method or field works, file answers carry their imports, `base_type_name` is filled, and unknown types and empty requests get proper `NOT_FOUND` / `INVALID_ARGUMENT` errors ([#283](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/283)).
- **Paced Kafka redelivery** — `@connectum/events-kafka` redelivers an unsettled message in order after a configurable pause (`consumerOptions.redeliveryDelay`, default 1 s), and `ack()` / `nack(false)` commit the consumer-group offset, so a restarted group resumes exactly where it stopped ([#299](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/299)).
- **One settlement per AMQP delivery** — a handler that calls `ack()` or `nack(false)` and then throws no longer makes `@connectum/events-amqp` settle the same delivery twice, which made RabbitMQ close the consumer channel and left the queue without a consumer; the first settlement wins and a later one is a silent no-op.
- **AMQP consumers that come back** — when RabbitMQ ends one subscription's consumer on a healthy connection (its queue was deleted, the consumer was cancelled, the channel was closed), `@connectum/events-amqp` now reports `consumer-lost` and restores it with backoff (`consumer-restored` / `consumer-restore-failed`) instead of leaving the subscription silent; a handler that throws synchronously is requeued instead of killing the channel, and `FakeAmqpAdapter` can simulate a lost consumer.
- **OpenTelemetry that survives a shutdown** — `shutdownProvider()` now releases the provider even when the collector is unreachable (the call still rejects, but `getProvider()` starts clean and a second call is a no-op), stops tracing, metrics and logs independently, and releases the OpenTelemetry API registrations it took (leaving anyone else's alone), so a provider created afterwards delivers metrics instead of silently recording into a no-op meter; interceptors created earlier follow the current provider.
- **A server that cannot be left half-started** — a `start` or `ready` listener that throws now fails `start()` and releases the port, the signal handlers and the event bus; a throwing `stopping` or `stop` listener no longer strands the server in `stopping` — the others still run, the exception is reported through `error`, and shutdown always ends in `stopped`.
- **A logger that never changes the call** — a log sink that throws no longer turns a successful response into `Internal` or replaces the real error; a failed call is logged as `RPC <path> failed with <Code>`, and a streamed response is timed until the stream really ends instead of when it was created.
- **A shutdown that keeps its budget** — on the Redis, Kafka and NATS adapters `EventBus.stop()` now honours `drainTimeout`: the subscriptions close while the handlers drain, instead of waiting for a stuck handler to be released by `handlerTimeout` (a 5 s budget used to mean about 30 s).
- **Publish that tells the truth about the connection** — `@connectum/events-amqp` rejects `publish()` with a typed `AmqpConnectionError` while the connection is not usable instead of a raw "Channel closed", a `connect()` superseded by `disconnect()` no longer leaves an orphan connection on the broker, and a non-finite or non-positive `publishTimeoutMs` falls back to 30000 ms instead of timing every publish out after a millisecond.
- **A scaffolder that refuses bad input** — `connectum init` now takes a destination path (the package name is its last segment), rejects names npm would reject, makes `--no-sample` produce a real config-only project, reports an unusable base as one list of defects and checks every write target before writing anything; `connectum proto sync` fails with the names of services reflection cannot describe and bounds each request with `--timeout`.
- **Redis redelivery that skips no entry** — one entry whose handler keeps failing no longer blocks the rest of a reclaimed batch, and the reclaim scan continues from the cursor `XAUTOCLAIM` returns, so stale entries behind a busy pending list are reached; failures are logged with the entry id.
- **Kafka handlers that may run long** — `@connectum/events-kafka` heartbeats in the background while a handler runs, so a handler slower than the consumer's `sessionTimeout` is no longer dropped from its group and its message redelivered forever.
- **Bad shutdown and read-limit options fail at creation** — `createServer()` now rejects a `shutdown.timeout` that is not an integer from 0 to 2147483647 (it used to fire after a millisecond and cut live connections) and `defineService()` rejects a `readMaxBytes` such as `NaN` (it used to disable the limit silently), each with an error naming the option.
- **Kafka commit strategy** — `@connectum/events-kafka` takes `consumerOptions.commitStrategy`: `"per-message"` (the default, unchanged) commits every acknowledged message, `"per-batch"` sends one offset commit per batch for throughput, at the price of a larger redelivery window that idempotent handlers absorb.
- **Logs without payloads by default** — `createLoggerInterceptor` no longer hands request and response bodies (which carry tokens and personal data) to the log sink; pass `includeBodies: true` to bring them back. Breaking for anyone who reads bodies from that output; see the migration guide.
- **Identity for the whole stream** — `getAuthContext()` / `requireAuthContext()` now return the verified caller in server-streaming and bidirectional handlers after the first `await` or `yield` and in `finally` (they used to return `undefined`, or over `server.localClient()` the identity of the in-process caller), for every `@connectum/auth` interceptor; cleanup after a cancel, deadline or shutdown runs under the call's own context.
- **Streaming handlers run inside their server span** — `createOtelInterceptor()` now makes the server span the active span for the whole of a server-streaming or bidirectional handler (start, after `await`, after `yield`, `finally`), so `traced()` and `startActiveSpan` in such handlers produce child spans of the call instead of detached ones; unary behaviour is unchanged.
- **Client-streaming catalog calls that tell the whole story** — `close()` on a `ctx.stream` or `createCatalogClient` client-streaming handle now waits for the call's final status instead of resolving at the first response: a failure after the response is reported rather than swallowed, a surplus response is rejected, and an OpenTelemetry client span finishes (it used to stay open forever). A server that delays its final status now holds `close()` until it arrives or the call is canceled.
- **One outgoing chain for every catalog route** — `outgoingInterceptors` now run on `ctx.call` / `ctx.stream` and `server.client()` whether the target is in-process, behind `remoteResolver` or mocked, and `createCatalogClient` takes its own chain; mount identity and tracing once (**BREAKING** only if you had duplicated the same policy on resolver transports).
- **Wildcard subscriptions that behave** — on `@connectum/events-nats` an event matched by several patterns of one subscription (`user.created`, `user.*`, `user.>`) is handled once instead of once per pattern, with no change to the consumers on the broker and no action on upgrade; on `@connectum/events-kafka` a catch-all `>` no longer subscribes the broker's internal `__consumer_offsets`, and `consumerOptions.topicDiscoveryInterval` (on by default, five minutes; `false` restores the fixed list) makes a Kafka wildcard pick up topics created after the subscription.
- **Unknown procedures answered in the protocol of the request** — a call to a procedure or service the server does not serve now returns `unimplemented` encoded as Connect (HTTP 501 with a JSON error, or an end-of-stream envelope), gRPC (`grpc-status: 12`) or gRPC-Web (a trailers frame) instead of a bare `404`; plain HTTP requests keep the `404`.
- **Timeouts that really cancel** — `createTimeoutInterceptor` now aborts `req.signal` / `ctx.signal` when its deadline expires or the caller cancels, and `createRetryInterceptor` stops its backoff and starts no further attempt, so a timed-out call no longer retries or returns a late success; repeated timeouts now count as circuit-breaker failures (**BREAKING** for code that relied on a late result — see the migration guide).
- **Plain-object requests in the service catalog** — a regenerated catalog accepts an object literal wherever a request message is expected (`context.call`, server-stream calls, client-stream and bidi `send`), type-checked against the schema, so `create()` is no longer required just to make a call. Breaking for code that reads a catalog request as a full message (`$typeName`, assignment to `MessageShape`); see the changeset for the one-line migration ([#331](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/331)).
- **AMQP wildcard routing matches the EventBus** — on a topic exchange `@connectum/events-amqp` now binds a terminal `>` as `*.#`, so `user.>` no longer receives the bare `user` key, exactly like the common matcher; subscriptions RabbitMQ would read differently (a complete `#` segment on a topic exchange, a non-terminal `>`, a complete `*` or `>` on a direct exchange when the adapter creates the binding) are rejected before any queue is declared, while fanout and headers exchanges keep accepting every pattern (the queue receives everything and the EventBus picks handlers). Existing `user.#` bindings are not removed automatically — replace them with `user.*.#` (**BREAKING** behaviour correction, see the AMQP migration guide) ([#329](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/329)).
- **Selective routing on an AMQP headers exchange** — `@connectum/events-amqp` no longer adds its catch-all binding to a queue whose `x-match` bindings you declare in `topology.bindings`, so a queue declared that way receives only the messages those bindings select instead of everything. Breaking for a queue that declared selective bindings and relied on receiving all messages: declare the binding without arguments to keep that. A durable queue that the previous version already bound keeps its old catch-all binding until you remove it (the migration steps are in the package README), so existing queues and new environments behave differently until then.
- **`connectum init --package-manager bun`** — the scaffolder now accepts `bun` next to `pnpm` and `npm`, independent of `--runtime`: a Bun-installed project runs on Node.js and an npm-installed one on Bun; install, typecheck and test are verified end to end ([#246](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/246)).
- **Redis RESP3 for the events adapter** — `@connectum/events-redis` moves to ioredis 6: RESP2 stays the default, RESP3 is opt-in with `redisOptions.protocol: 3` (and `replyMapping`), and the stream replies the adapter depends on (`XREADGROUP`, `XAUTOCLAIM`, `XPENDING`) are validated and normalized, with Redis 6.2 and Valkey covered by broker tests ([#254](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/254)).
- **AMQP subscriptions work on RabbitMQ 4.3** — the private queue of a subscription without `group` is now exclusive to the subscriber's connection by default (`consumerOptions.exclusive`, default `true`), because RabbitMQ 4.3 refuses a queue that is neither durable nor exclusive and the subscription used to fail with a closed channel (541); subscriptions with `group` are unaffected ([#307](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/307)).
- **Cancelling a stream releases the handler** — cancelling a streaming call (client abort, deadline, shutdown) now finishes the handler's output on both transports, so a handler parked at `yield` reaches its `finally` and its cursors, subscriptions and handles are released; before, an in-process call, and on Node 26.10 and Bun an HTTP/2 call, left the handler suspended ([#309](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/309)).
- **JWT access tokens must carry `exp`** — `createJwtAuthInterceptor` and `signedTokenTrust` now reject a signed token without an expiration claim (RFC 9068), so a token that never expires can no longer authenticate a call; set `requireExpiration: false` on the interceptor options or the issuer entry to keep the old behaviour while you re-issue tokens (**BREAKING** for issuers that mint tokens without `exp` — see the migration guide) ([#348](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/348)).
- **Strict gateway CIDR matching** — the gateway-trust allow-list in `@connectum/auth` now parses IPv4 addresses and `/prefix` lengths per RFC 791 and RFC 4632: a malformed block (`10.0.0.0/33`, `010.0.0.1`, `10.0.0/8`) matches nothing but its own literal text instead of trusting an unintended range ([#344](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/344)).
- **A repeated `stop()` is a no-op** — calling `server.stop()` on a server that is already stopped resolves without an error, so shutdown handlers and `autoShutdown` can overlap safely; calling it before `start()` still fails ([#347](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/347)).
- **RPC telemetry follows the current OpenTelemetry conventions** — spans and metrics now carry `rpc.system.name="connectrpc"`, a fully qualified `rpc.method` (`acme.v1.Greeter/SayHello`) and a string `rpc.response.status_code` (`OK` or the Connect error-code name) instead of `rpc.system`, `rpc.service` and the numeric `rpc.connect_rpc.status_code`, so conventions-aware backends read Connectum telemetry without mapping. Update dashboards, alerts and queries that use the old names (Prometheus labels `rpc_system`, `rpc_service`, `rpc_connect_rpc_status_code`); the renamed TypeScript constants are listed in the changeset.
- **Usable RPC latency histograms** — `rpc.server.call.duration` and `rpc.client.call.duration` now use the explicit second-scale bucket boundaries from the OpenTelemetry RPC metrics specification (`0.005 ... 10`, exported as `RPC_DURATION_BUCKETS`) instead of the SDK default millisecond scale that put every call into the first bucket. The `le` bucket edges of these two histograms change, so update dashboards and alerts that reference the old edges; other boundaries need your own `MeterProvider` with a `View` (see the metrics guide).
- **AMQP publishing survives a channel-only close** — when RabbitMQ closes just the publish channel (a publish to a missing exchange, a `406`), the next `publish()` opens a new channel on the same connection instead of failing until the next reconnect; the `publish-channel-lost` and `publish-channel-restored` lifecycle events report it, and `publishRetry` never retries the refused publish.
- **Kafka adapter options without client-library types** — the public options of `@connectum/events-kafka` are now Connectum-owned types (`ssl`, `sasl`, timeouts, `retry`, `logLevel`, `compression` by name), so the Kafka client library can be replaced without breaking the package API; settings that have no portable form go in `clientOptions`. **Breaking:** the `kafkaConfig` option is removed and now throws; the changeset has the old-to-new table.
- **Kafka consumer lifecycle events** — `KafkaAdapter` accepts `lifecycle.onLifecycle` and reports a crashed consumer (`consumer-lost`), the failed attempts to bring it back and its return to the group (`consumer-restored`), plus the producer's first connect; the same pattern as the AMQP adapter, nothing changes without the option.
- **Redis connection lifecycle events** — `RedisAdapter` accepts `lifecycle.onLifecycle` and reports `connected`, `disconnected` (once per loss of each connection), `reconnecting` and the terminal `reconnect-failed`, the same pattern as the AMQP adapter; without the option nothing changes.
- **NATS connection lifecycle events** — `NatsAdapter` accepts `lifecycle.onLifecycle` and reports `connected`, `disconnected`, `reconnecting` and the terminal `reconnect-failed`, the same pattern as the AMQP adapter, so a lost or abandoned NATS connection can be alerted on; without the option nothing changes.
- **Error text stays on the server** — `errorHandler` no longer sends the text of a non-Connect failure to the client: a thrown `Error` or string reaches it as `Internal` / `internal error`, and the original stays in `cause`, `onError` and the log; `exposeErrorMessages: true` brings the old behavior back (**BREAKING** for clients that parse those texts).
- **Descriptor mocks that match real descriptors** — `createMockDescMessage` and the other `@connectum/test-fixtures` mocks (also exported by `@connectum/testing`) now follow protobuf-es: `create(mock)` zero-initialises declared fields, snake_case names give camelCase `localName`, a repeated field number throws and reserved RPC names get `$`. Tests that compared `create(mock)` with a bare `{ $typeName }` or used snake_case lookups need a one-line update (**BREAKING** for those tests, see the migration guide). The fixtures also refuse input they used to swallow: an unknown scalar `type` (`"strng"` is no longer a `string` field), a field number outside the protobuf range, an unknown method kind, a second `register` of one method and an unusable delay now throw with the argument named, and `createMockFn` forwards `this` and records each call's result and error like `node:test`.
- **HTTP health asks about the service you name** — `/healthz?service=<name>` in `@connectum/healthcheck` no longer falls back to the overall state when the request carries an empty or malformed `Host` header, and `Healthcheck()` now rejects an empty or malformed `httpPaths` instead of silently serving nothing (**BREAKING** for `httpPaths: []`: use `httpEnabled: false`).
- **Auth configuration fails loudly** — `@connectum/auth` now throws on a misspelled proto `policy` / `default_policy`, on a method that is both `public` and `internal`, on `skipMethods: ["*"]`, and on a cache `ttl` that is not finite or a `maxSize` below 1; with `propagateHeaders` an identity holding NUL, CR or LF is rejected as `Unauthenticated` before it is cached; and `signedTokenTrust` identifies a caller by its verified `iss`, reading `sub` and `scope` only through an explicit `claimsMapping` (**BREAKING** for those configurations — see the `auth-proto-options` migration guide).
- **Spans no longer claim `OK`** — `@connectum/otel` leaves the span status unset on success, as the OpenTelemetry specification and `otelconnect-go` do, and sets `ERROR` only on failure; a stream whose consumer stops early also stays unset. Queries and alerts that select `status = ok` must switch to "status is not error" (**BREAKING** for them); cancellation stays spelled `CANCELED`.
- **Interceptor options fail at startup instead of misbehaving** — the numeric options of `timeout`, `bulkhead`, `circuitBreaker` and the `retry` delays (`initialDelay`, `maxDelay`) must be integers (delays at most 2147483647 ms, which the platform timer cannot exceed; `retry.maxRetries` keeps accepting finite fractions), `createDefaultInterceptors` refuses `null`, numbers, strings and `fallback: true` with a `TypeError` naming the key instead of silently leaving the interceptor off, and `connectum init --resilience` no longer offers `fallback`. The bulkhead refusal text now states its configured limits. **Breaking** for configurations that passed fractional or oversized values, `fallback: true` or `null`; the changeset and the migration guide have the replacements.
- **`proto sync --from` reads the address by its shape** — a bare `host:port` always gets `http://` (`httpbin.local:5000` no longer fails with `Invalid URL`), `http://` and `https://` URLs are used as typed in any letter case, and any other scheme such as `ftp://h:5` is refused before a connection with a message that names it.
- **`proto sync` ends when its work ends** — `connectum proto sync` now exits as soon as the descriptors are fetched instead of waiting out the time limit of its last reflection request (10 seconds by default), the new `--timeout` accepts 1 to 99999999 ms (the longest limit an eight-digit `grpc-timeout` header can carry), and a failed write of the descriptor file no longer leaves its temporary directory behind.
- **Fallback response accepted by every protocol** — the response synthesised by the fallback interceptor carries only the protocol headers it needs, and gRPC, gRPC-web and HTTP/1.1 chunked clients now accept it.
- **Fallback never answers a refusal of access** — a failure with the code `Unauthenticated` or `PermissionDenied` is rethrown as it is and the fallback handler is not called for it, wherever the authentication or authorization interceptor stands in the chain ([#419](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/419)).
- **AMQP publish without the 40 ms stall** — `@connectum/events-amqp` turns Nagle's algorithm off on its connections by default; a `publish()` that follows the delivery of the previous message on the same connection took 43.9 ms at the median in a measurement against RabbitMQ 4.3.6 and now takes 0.4 ms. `socketOptions: { noDelay: false }` restores amqplib's behaviour ([#418](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/418)).
- **Publishing to a malformed topic names the topic** — `publish()` of the NATS and in-memory adapters throws a `TypeError` for a topic with an empty segment (`""`, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `.`), and the Kafka adapter does so for its reserved names (`""`, `.`, `..`), before anything reaches the broker; NATS used to answer `jetstream is not enabled` and the in-memory adapter delivered the event to wildcard subscribers. It is the publishing side of the check `subscribe()` already makes.
- **Handlers that finish during shutdown acknowledge their message** — `@connectum/events-redis` and `@connectum/events-amqp` no longer tear down the acknowledgement path when `unsubscribe()` runs, which `EventBus.stop()` does before it waits for the handlers: on Redis the acknowledgement used to fail with `Connection is closed.` and the entry came back after 30 seconds, on RabbitMQ the broker took the message back and delivered it again to a consumer of the same group.
- **Telemetry never breaks the call it wraps** — `traced`, `traceAll` and the OpenTelemetry interceptors keep the call's outcome whatever `recordArgs` receives or a thrown value is; an invalid `OTEL_BSP_*` count variable now warns (`CONNECTUM_OTEL_INVALID_ENV`) and falls back to the default instead of failing provider creation ([#417](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/417)).
- **Inputs that used to be undefined now have an answer** — `errorHandler` accepts only Connect codes 1 to 16 (anything else becomes `Internal`), `PORT` must be an integer, `connectum generate service` refuses names it used to rewrite silently, a TLS key without a certificate (or the reverse) is an error instead of a silent switch to the directory files, and `subscribe()` rejects empty subject tokens that NATS cannot serve ([#417](https://github.com/Connectum-Framework/connectum/pull/417)).
- **No new work after a shutdown begins** — the event bus now stops receiving when the server's shutdown signal aborts: a message that arrives before the bus hook runs is returned to the broker instead of starting a handler with an already cancelled `ctx.signal`, so it is not dead-lettered by a retry that can no longer happen; handlers that are running finish as before (**BREAKING** behaviour for services with an `eventBus`).
- **One-line service selection from the environment** — `enabledServices: enabledServicesFromEnv(process.env.CONNECTUM_SERVICES)` in `@connectum/core` mounts every supplied service when the variable is unset or empty and only the named ones when it lists them, instead of the empty list `parseServicesEnv` returns for an unset variable, which mounts none; `enabledServices` also accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.
- **`async` error hooks cannot crash the server** — a rejecting `async` `onError` of the error handler interceptor no longer ends the Node process with an unhandled rejection; the first failure is logged once.
- **Fallback no longer hides validation errors** — with `fallback` enabled in `createDefaultInterceptors`, a request that breaks a validation rule is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` again instead of being answered with the fallback value; validation now stands outside the fallback.
- **Trustworthy RPC telemetry values** — `@connectum/otel` now reports real message sizes with protobuf-es v2 (they were always `0`), records the duration of a streaming call when the stream ends instead of at the response head, puts `error.type` and `rpc.response.status_code` on a stream that fails mid-way, marks a server span `ERROR` only for the server-class Connect codes (`NOT_FOUND` and the other caller outcomes leave it unset), and no longer fails an RPC when your `filter` or `attributeFilter` throws; `traced()` / `traceAll()` keep the span of a generator open while it is iterated and `traceAll()` no longer breaks getters over `#private` fields, `Map.size` or frozen objects. Dashboards that read sizes, streaming durations or server span status will see different values (see the RPC telemetry migration page).
- **Reflection that lets a server stop** — `server.stop()` no longer waits out `shutdown.timeout` for a client that keeps a `ServerReflectionInfo` stream open (grpcurl in interactive mode, an IDE plugin, Postman); the reflection service can be described through itself (`grpcurl describe grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection`); and an error answer repeats at most 128 characters of a requested name instead of the whole of it.
- **Health.Watch shows every status change** — a service set `NOT_SERVING` and back inside one `watchInterval` used to be invisible to watchers; `Health.Watch` now sends each change in order as soon as the manager reports it (new `HealthcheckManager.subscribe()`), and `Healthcheck()` and the manager refuse an unusable `watchInterval`, a bad `manager` or `httpEnabled`, a second `Healthcheck()` in one server, and any status outside the four `ServingStatus` values (**BREAKING** for configurations that relied on the old silent acceptance — see the migration guide).
- **Redis consumers that survive data loss** — `@connectum/events-redis` re-creates a consumer group that Redis lost (restart without persistence, `FLUSHALL`, failover to an empty replica) instead of logging `NOGROUP` forever, reads from the start of the stream so every entry Redis still retains is delivered (entries `maxLen` trimmed meanwhile are gone), and reports the new `group-recreated` lifecycle event.
- **AMQP adapter: checked options** — `AmqpAdapter()` rejects options that cannot work (an unknown `topologyMode` used to act as `assert` and declare the topology) with an error that names the option, and the new opt-in `consumerOptions.redeliveryDelay` spaces out redeliveries of a message whose handler keeps throwing.
- **Kafka wildcard subscriptions survive a deleted topic** — deleting one topic a wildcard matched no longer stalls the healthy ones for about five minutes: `@connectum/events-kafka` replaces the crashed consumer with one that subscribes the topics that remain, and reports `consumer-lost` then `consumer-restored`.
- **AMQP adapter: start-up that can be cancelled** — `disconnect()` now ends a `connect()` that still waits for an unreachable broker. It never settled before, so a server with an event bus stayed in `starting` and the process could not exit on its own; the cancelled `connect()` rejects with `AmqpConnectionError` and leaves no retry timer behind.
- **Gateway interceptor no longer forwards forged identity headers** — `createGatewayAuthInterceptor` deletes the standard `x-auth-*` identity headers after reading its input, so with `propagateHeaders: true` a client-supplied `x-auth-roles`, `x-auth-scopes`, `x-auth-name` or `x-auth-claims` can no longer reach a downstream service that trusts them; a CIDR block in `trustSource` now needs `allowCallerControlledCidr: true`, an identity that does not fit its `x-auth-*` headers is refused instead of cut, and Cyrillic, CJK and emoji names are propagated encoded instead of rejected (see the auth identity migration page).
- **NATS adapter that recovers and explains itself** — `@connectum/events-nats` resumes a subscription after its JetStream stream was deleted and created again (it used to stay silent for good), checks its options at creation (`servers`, `ackWait`, `maxDeliver`, `deliverPolicy`), logs the delivery that uses up `maxDeliver`, adds the opt-in `consumerOptions.redeliveryDelay` and `prefetch`, delivers `x-*` and empty metadata like the other adapters, and names the topic or the servers in connect, publish and subscribe timeouts.
- **A wrong OpenTelemetry variable no longer fails every RPC** — `@connectum/otel` ignores an empty, mis-cased or unknown `OTEL_*_EXPORTER`, protocol or endpoint value with a `CONNECTUM_OTEL_INVALID_ENV` process warning instead of throwing inside the first instrumented call; `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is percent-decoded, `initProvider({ settings })` rejects a misspelled exporter with `TypeError`, a concurrent `shutdownProvider()` waits for the flush, and `shutdownProvider({ timeout })` bounds it.
- **A scaffolded project that works and says what it needs** — a `connectum init --auth` project serves gRPC Health and reflection without a token (so `connectum proto sync` works against it), `--no-healthcheck` leaves no Docker `HEALTHCHECK` on `/healthz`, and the generated README names the environment and broker the auth and events modules need. The CLI refuses unknown flags, `generate service` outside a project and `proto sync` failures read as one line; `protoc-gen-connectum-catalog` requires `target=ts` and refuses a repeated `output_file` (**BREAKING** for scripts that relied on the silent acceptance).
- **Test server on loopback, parity scenarios that mean what they say** — `createTestServer()` listens on `127.0.0.1` instead of all interfaces (pass `host: '0.0.0.0'` to reach it from another container; **BREAKING** for tests that do), takes `shutdown: { timeout }` to bound `close()`, and rejects services, interceptors and protocols of the wrong type with the option named; `transportParityTest` no longer fails on protocol headers or on measured durations, `InMemoryMetricCollector.flush()` returns only new data, `createMockContext` takes `method` and `signal`, and a failing `mockService` implementation keeps its message and `cause`.
- **OpenTelemetry exports by default, as the specification says** — with no `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` or `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `@connectum/otel` now sends telemetry over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf) to `http://localhost:4318` instead of printing it to standard output. This is a breaking change: set the variables to `console` to keep the old output, or `none` to switch a signal off. A collector that is not there no longer floods the log: an identical export failure is printed once a minute.
- **OpenTelemetry logs no longer lost in bursts** — `@connectum/otel` exports OTLP log records in batches (`OTEL_BLRP_*`) instead of one request per record: 100 records emitted at once to a collector that answers in 100 ms used to deliver 10; now all arrive, up to `OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY` (1000 ms) later, and `shutdownProvider()` sends the queue. The `console` exporter still prints each record at once.
- **A cut stream says so** — when `server.stop()` ends a server stream that is still sending, the client now gets the messages already sent and then an `unavailable` error, instead of a normal end of stream that looked like a complete list (Connect and gRPC clients, and in-process calls); a handler that returns by itself after seeing the abort still ends the call normally.
- **Fail-closed auth configuration** — `@connectum/auth` refuses a misspelled `defaultPolicy` or rule `effect`, an empty JWT `issuer`/`audience`, method patterns that never match and unusable gateway options when an interceptor is created; `authorize` allows only on `true`, a JWT needs a non-empty string subject, and an `internal` proto method without `requires` is open only to an identity from `createInternalAuthInterceptor` (**BREAKING** for configurations that relied on any of these).
